failedGate: B1: Basketball credibility; universal player turnover splits lack stable support. This component prerequisite cannot pass complete-game gates.
hypothesis: Player turnover tendency is a cost per combined shooting/passing workload, not a per-minute rate with a universal turnover split. Normalizing observed turnovers by combined prior role exposure improves transport without shrinkage.
formula: For each player let s=priorShots/priorLeagueShots, a=priorAssists/priorLeagueAssists, t=priorTOV/priorLeagueTOV, beta=passingWeight. demand=(1-beta)*s+beta*a; costRatio=t/demand. With prior league turnover share q, per-allocated-shot TOV cost=q/(1-q)*(1-beta)*costRatio and per-passing-unit TOV cost=q*beta*costRatio. Requested shares remain proportional to prior rates times target minutes. Allocate100 passing units first, then shots and their turnover costs from the remaining100 event budget.
distinction: No shrinkage, minute-based reliability or changed target for candidate1. Player shot/passing turnover fractions now depend on their prior workload mix; at nominal observed exposure the two components reconstruct prior TOV. beta0 is exactly the frozen shot-only control. No causal passing skill is claimed.
unsupported: Nonpositive demand, missing/nonfinite costs, empty shot/passing demand or passing costs exceeding100 events are unsupported. Zero assist exposure is never filled. At beta0 use the original shot-only result for exact control replay.
fixedInputs: Original prior rates, prior league context, actual target-minute weights, fallback rules, source team labels and 100 synthetic passing units. No target TOV, shots or assists enter predictions; only actual target minutes are conditioned on. No capacities or points model.
cohort: Original team-study common support only; freeze membership before evaluation. A new unsupported training row invalidates that configuration; never drop rows. Report every attempted training result.
selection: Minimum equal-team training RMSE among fully supported configurations; exact ties choose smaller passingWeight. Save a separate selection artifact before evaluating any new later candidate prediction. Evaluate only the selected weight later; no subset or later selection.
comparison: Equal-team RMSE/MAE/bias and paired MSE normal95 intervals clustered by target season, as in the frozen team study. Earlier statistics are selection evidence, not independent validation. All later years were previously exposed.
proceedRules: Selected passingWeight is positive and every originally common-support row remains supported.
Selected training RMSE is no higher than unchanged shot-only training RMSE.
On all later teams, selected RMSE is at least2% lower than EACH of unchanged shot-only and unshrunk split-role, and EACH paired MSE interval upper bound is below zero.
On later teams with at least90% prior-minute coverage, selected RMSE is no higher than EITHER unchanged baseline. Report subgroup uncertainty without claiming significance.
failureAction: Any failed or unmeasurable rule rejects candidate2 at the component gate. The two-mechanism budget is exhausted: keep live balance and stop modeling. Present an explicit scope/target/model decision; any new cycle requires user approval. No grid expansion, third candidate or fresh-family consumption.
successAction: Advance only to complete-candidate integration assessment, not release. If no complete-game finalist can meet the existing gates within scope, stop and request an explicit decision. Fresh-family expectations still need approval before measurement.
limits: Combined role exposure and fixed100 passing units remain design assumptions, not measured passes or causal responsibility.
Uncapped season aggregates with observed target minutes are neither five-player units nor preseason forecasts.
Explicit league fallback stays unchanged; missing old-era data are not newly imputed or dropped from release requirements.
No changes to peaks, shooting efficiency, defense, reserves, coaches, scores, wins, live rules or save schemas.
This uses the second and final mechanism under scorecard1, including rejection at a cheap component gate.
